newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel traffic resumes after three-hour strike.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel traffic resumes after three-hour strike.

text.p: Strikers blocked tourist and truck traffic through the tunnel linking France and Britain for three hours on Wednesday in a protest at working conditions.
Drivers sat in their vehicles in stifling sunshine as the stoppage, the first major action by Eurotunnel unions, created tailbacks several km (miles) long at the French terminal.
No Shuttle rail services left Coquelles during the strike and and only one train carrying trucks departed.
At the British end of the tunnel at Folkestone, Shuttle services were running late and shrank to just one departure every hour.
French strikers lifted pickets at toll booths at around 5 p.m. (1500 GMT) after winning a management promise of talks later in the day to review working conditions.
Officials said that few workers heeded the strike call overall.
Freight traffic and Eurostar passenger trains, run by the state railways SNCF, were not hit by the action.

The unions are demanding better working conditions and accuse management of ignoring grievances over salaries and working hours. They have proposed meeting management representatives, who have suggested July 29 for a first round of talks.
Eurotunnel employs just over 3,000 staff, including 1,600 French workers.
